chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who carries the goods for the people of the market and they have established a price upon it, so they are saying, ‘Sell, and whatever is the increase, so it is for you’. He (peace be upon him) said: ‘There is no problem with that, but he cannot sell them for profit (sharing basis)’.

key_terms.قَوَّمُوهُ: They appraised / set a price for it
key_terms.مُرَابَحَةً: Profit-sharing / Murabahah (a specific type of trade partnership)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on an agent keeping the surplus from selling goods at a higher price than agreed?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates the 'what you add is yours' model for market agents, distinguishing it from 'murabahah' (often interpreted in this context as a specific type of partnership or markup arrangement) to prevent ambiguity in agency contracts. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on clarity in commercial transactions, ensuring that the agent's profit is derived from surplus value rather than a fixed percentage of the principal, thereby aligning with the principles of *bay'* (sale) over *mudarabah* (profit-sharing) in this specific agency scenario. The distinction highlights the scholarly nuance in defining permissible agency (*wakalah*) versus partnership (*shirkah*) structures in early Islamic markets.
